name: Resorcinol monoacetate

lead: Resorcinol monoacetate is an acetate ester of resorcinol that has been used in dermatological products as a keratolytic, meaning it helps loosen and shed dead skin cells. It was listed in the National Formulary in 1946, and a 1973 paper describes measuring it in dermatological products.

Its appearance relevance is clearer skin and exfoliation: resorcinol-type ingredients appear in acne products, and the monoacetate has been compounded for hidradenitis suppurativa. Research on this specific ester is sparse.

paras: It is applied topically as part of compounded or commercial creams and lotions, often alongside other keratolytic or anti-acne ingredients. Clinicians prescribe it as a compounded preparation for particular skin conditions.

Resorcinol compounds can irritate skin and carry hazard statements for skin and eye irritation. In 2022 the EU named resorcinol a substance of very high concern because of endocrine-disrupting properties.

angle.text: As a keratolytic, resorcinol monoacetate is used in skin preparations to help exfoliate the surface, with acne and seborrhea as traditional targets.

lead: Resorcinol monoacetate, also called monoacetylresorcinol and sold as Euresol, is an acetylated form of resorcinol used in dermatology as a keratolytic [1]. It was the subject of a 1946 bulletin of the American Pharmaceutical Association's National Formulary committee, and a 1973 paper describes gas chromatography for measuring it in dermatological products [2][3].

For looks, the parent compound resorcinol is an over-the-counter acne ingredient at 2 percent or less, with higher strengths in prescription treatments, and was used by the British Army for chronic acne in the 1950s and early 1960s [1]. Resorcinol monoacetate has been compounded at 10 or 15 percent for hidradenitis suppurativa, and the Wikipedia article says evidence for this use is growing [1].
Published clinical research on resorcinol monoacetate itself is very limited.

paras: Resorcinol is in OTC acne products at 2 percent or less [1]. Resorcinol monoacetate has been used in dermatological preparations for exfoliation [2][3].

Resorcinol monoacetate is compounded at 10 or 15 percent for new active lesions in Hurley Stage I or II hidradenitis suppurativa, applied for a few weeks, according to Wikipedia's resorcinol article [1].

Resorcinol has low toxicity compared with phenol but carries GHS hazard statements for oral toxicity, skin irritation and serious eye damage, and in 2022 the EU named it a substance of very high concern under REACH for endocrine-disrupting properties [1].
A 1946 National Formulary committee bulletin lists resorcinol monoacetate [2], and a 1973 paper describes quantitative gas-liquid chromatography of it in dermatological products [3].
